title: Thumbtack vs Angi for Contractors: How Leads Are Billed
summary: Thumbtack vs Angi for contractors: how each platform matches, charges and budgets for leads, from their own help pages, and how to answer both fast.
body_markdown:
Thumbtack and Angi both send homeowners to local contractors, but they bill those contacts on different rules. A lead you already paid for still needs a fast reply. This guide maps how each platform charges — without dollar amounts — and what to verify before you raise spend on either one.


Neither marketplace guarantees a booked job. Both reward pros who respond quickly when several companies receive the same request. If you run paid leads alongside a listing, see[Google Business Profile for contractors](https://sameday.ai/post/google-business-profile-for-contractors) . For phone coverage options after the lead arrives, see[virtual assistant for contractors](https://sameday.ai/post/virtual-assistant-for-contractors) . For job board handoffs after the booking, see[restoration software](https://sameday.ai/post/restoration-software) .


## How Thumbtack charges for leads


On Thumbtack, you pay for leads — customers who reach out to you — and for Opportunities, also called open leads ([how much you pay](https://help.thumbtack.com/article/pay-for-leads) ,[types of leads](https://help.thumbtack.com/article/types-of-leads) ).


### Direct leads


Direct leads come from customers who found you in search and chose to contact you. When a new lead arrives and the job matches your preferences, Thumbtack auto-charges at the lead price that applies to your account. Some accounts set an exact price per service; others use smarter lead matching and set a minimum and maximum price range per trade, then pay within that range based on the job's estimated value ([budget](https://help.thumbtack.com/article/set-budget) ,[lead prices](https://help.thumbtack.com/article/set-lead-prices) ). That setup is separate from Smart Match, an optional control that can send and charge for direct leads outside your saved service and area preferences. If the job is wrong for your trade or area, review the lead details and decline it before you reply—replying first can block an automatic refund on unsuitable direct leads. With Sameday auto-reply on Thumbtack enabled, a customer message can trigger a reply before you review or decline, and the refund may not apply. You also choose a weekly budget that covers lead spend across services. Lead cost varies by job type, size, market, and how many pros are available. Actual weekly spend can land above or below the budget estimate depending on demand.


If a lead costs more than what is left in the weekly budget, Thumbtack can still charge the full lead price up to a platform-defined over-budget limit, then pause new direct leads until the budget resets on Monday—unless Lead boosts are turned on, which can send and charge additional direct leads after the budget is reached. Opportunity charges do not draw from the weekly budget; they bill separately when you pursue them.


### Opportunities on Thumbtack


Opportunities are customers who started conversations with other pros but have not hired anyone yet ([Opportunities](https://help.thumbtack.com/article/opportunities) ). The fee shows upfront. You pay only if you reach out and the customer responds to your message. An Opportunity closes after 48 hours, after five pros express interest, or if the customer cancels. Thumbtack also lists preset jobs with no upfront lead cost and a take-home fee taken from the job price instead — a different product from standard leads.


Sources:[Thumbtack lead pricing](https://help.thumbtack.com/article/pay-for-leads) and[lead types](https://help.thumbtack.com/article/types-of-leads) .


## How Angi charges for leads


One homeowner request can match several pros on Angi and Thumbtack.


Angi separates Opportunities and leads. Lead fees vary by task, homeowner location, and demand ([Opportunities and Leads FAQ](https://intercom.help/angi/en/articles/6221483-opportunities-and-leads-frequently-asked-questions) ).


### Opportunities vs leads on Angi


An Opportunity is a homeowner project that matches your services and location. You review project details and the lead fee before showing interest. An Opportunity becomes a lead when both you and the homeowner show interest in connecting; that mutual interest is when Angi charges the lead fee. If you do not respond, the Opportunity does not become a lead and you are not charged.


Leads you receive automatically under a monthly budget are different. With that setup, Angi sends leads that match your services when a homeowner shows interest in your business. You are charged for those automatic leads whether or not you open or respond to them. Subscription contracts set the monthly budget annually. In the account you can pause automatic leads; changing covered tasks or ZIP codes on a subscription requires contacting Angi support.


### Monthly budget and extras


Your monthly budget is the amount you plan to spend on automatic leads for each budget cycle. That cycle resets on the anniversary of the date you were approved to join the Angi network, not on a calendar month. Only automatic leads count toward it. The final automatic lead before the budget is used up can bill above what is left in the monthly budget. On an annual subscription, contact Angi support to change the monthly budget amount. Opportunities you browse and accept manually are charged in addition to the monthly budget when both sides show interest. Opportunities and leads are not guaranteed jobs; Angi's help center says you still need to follow up with the homeowner to win the work.


Sources:[Angi Opportunities and Leads](https://intercom.help/angi/en/articles/6221483-opportunities-and-leads-frequently-asked-questions) .

## Speed decides both


Angi matches a project request with no more than five pros. On Thumbtack, an Opportunity closes after five pros express interest, but additional pros may still receive direct leads on the same project. Shared distribution means the homeowner often hires the first credible response, not the lowest lead fee.


Thumbtack's help center lists response speed among factors that affect how many direct leads you receive. Angi's FAQ says the faster you respond on Opportunities, the better your chance of winning the job. Automatic Angi leads still bill when they land, so slow follow-up spends budget without a conversation.


## Five-step marketplace check


Run this on Thumbtack and Angi before you raise either budget. It does not assume a response-time benchmark.


Five steps before you raise marketplace spend


1.


Open each vendor's own pricing page


Write how direct leads, Opportunities, and automatic leads bill on Thumbtack and Angi. Leave dollar amounts on the platform.


2.


List who answers each inbox


Name the person or system for Thumbtack messages and Angi notifications after 6 p.m. and on Saturday.


3.


Test automatic leads and Opportunities separately


On each platform, inspect one genuine automatic or direct lead and note whether you were charged on arrival. Then accept one Opportunity and note whether billing happens only after mutual interest.


4.


Time the first human or AI response


Record when Thumbtack gets an in-app reply and when Angi gets a call or text back.


5.


Confirm where the job lands


Check whether a booked visit appears in ServiceTitan or Housecall Pro during the conversation, or only in email later.


Keep the notes. They are the baseline before you change budgets on either marketplace.

## FAQ


### How does Thumbtack charge for leads?


On Thumbtack, you set either an exact lead price per service or a min–max range per trade on smarter lead matching, plus a weekly budget. Direct leads from search auto-pay at the applicable lead price when the lead arrives. With Lead boosts enabled, Thumbtack can keep sending direct leads after the weekly budget is reached. Opportunities show the fee upfront; you pay only if you reach out and the customer responds. Opportunity charges are separate from the weekly budget.


### How does Angi charge for leads?


Angi lead fees vary by task, homeowner location, and demand. An Opportunity becomes a lead when both you and the homeowner show interest; that is when you are charged. With automatic leads under a monthly budget, you are charged whether or not you open or respond to the lead. The monthly budget resets on the anniversary of your Angi network approval date, and the last automatic lead can exceed what is left. Changing covered tasks or ZIPs on a subscription requires contacting Angi support; you can pause automatic leads in the account. Opportunities you accept manually are charged in addition to the monthly budget.


### How many pros receive the same Angi lead?


Angi's help center says each homeowner project request is matched with no more than five pros, depending on lead type and location. The same cap applies to Opportunities.


### Are Thumbtack Opportunities shared with other pros?


Yes. Opportunities are customers who already contacted other pros but have not hired anyone yet. Thumbtack shows how many pros contacted the customer and how many responded. An Opportunity closes after 48 hours, after five pros express interest, or if the customer cancels.


### Does Sameday work with Thumbtack and Angi?


Yes. On Thumbtack, Sameday replies inside Thumbtack, then calls and texts the customer back. For Angi, Sameday answers Angi calls and leads immediately and keeps following up by call and text until there is an answer either way. Sameday does not reply inside Angi.


### Does Sameday book into ServiceTitan or Housecall Pro?


Yes. Sameday is a Certified ServiceTitan app and also integrates with Housecall Pro. Qualified marketplace jobs can be written into ServiceTitan or Housecall Pro during the conversation, per your playbook rules.
